page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.2xlarge is an x86_64 virtualization instance managed by the KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual processor. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring persistence to be managed through external network block storage volumes. It does not feature hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addressing.

With its pronounced 1:8 core-to-memory balance, the architecture prioritizes memory capacity over compute concurrency. This resource profile prevents organizations from provisioning excess computational cores simply to meet in-memory working set thresholds. Compute throughput remains constrained to the dual-thread capacity of its dedicated processors, making the platform unsuited for heavy parallel computation, vector processing, or local disk-intensive caching.

The ecs.s2.2xlarge is architected for small to mid-sized workloads requiring higher memory-to-CPU densities, including in-memory databases, Redis caches, staging environments, lightweight application middleware, and memory-bound background queues.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.s2.2xlarge is a memory-oriented virtual machine operating on the KVM hypervisor using an x86_64 architecture. The platform delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. It operates with zero local storage volumes and contains no discrete graphics hardware or complimentary public IPv4 assignments, relying exclusively on network-attached block storage for persistent data operations. Because the instance balances a light CPU footprint with substantial memory headroom, it avoids the resource inefficiency of paying for unneeded vCPUs just to acquire adequate RAM. Hardware performance is focused on memory residency rather than parallel computation. Consequently, the ecs.s2.2xlarge is suited for memory-intensive low-concurrency workloads, such as distributed in-memory data stores, caching layers, lightweight enterprise middleware, and staging environments.
